The '''64th Academy Awards''' ceremony, presented by the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] (AMPAS), honored the best [[1991 in film|films of 1991]] in the United States and took place on March 30, 1992, at the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]] in [[Los Angeles]] beginning at 6:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PST]] / 9:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|EST]]. During the ceremony, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences presented [[Academy Awards]] (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 23 categories. The ceremony, televised in the United States by [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], was produced by [[Gil Cates]] and directed by [[Jeff Margolis]]. Actor [[Billy Crystal]] hosted the show for the third consecutive year.<ref>{{cite news |title=Billy Crystal: Academy glad to have him back |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=16ksAAAAIBAJ&pg=1634,2531033 |access-date=September 5, 2013 |work=[[Star-News]] |date=February 8, 1992 |page=2A |archive-date=February 25, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210225001703/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=16ksAAAAIBAJ&pg=1634,2531033 |url-status=live }}</ref> Three weeks earlier, in a ceremony held at the [[Century Plaza Hotel]] in Los Angeles on March 7, the [[Academy Award for Technical Achievement|Academy Awards for Technical Achievement]] were presented by host [[Tom Hanks]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Past Scientific & Technical Awards Ceremonies |url=http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html |access-date=July 31, 2013 |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140213185729/http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html |archive-date=February 13, 2014}}</ref>

''[[The Silence of the Lambs (film)|The Silence of the Lambs]]'' won five awards, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hall |first1=Carla |title=The Triumph of the Lambs |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1992/03/31/the-triumph-of-the-lambs/afbc3636-881a-4918-ba0f-eb11045f7175/ |access-date=February 4, 2020 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=March 31, 1992 |archive-date=June 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190613163554/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1992/03/31/the-triumph-of-the-lambs/afbc3636-881a-4918-ba0f-eb11045f7175/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Pristin |first=Terry |title='Silence of the Lambs' Sweeps 5 Major Oscars : Movies: Thriller is only the third film to take all key categories. Palance, Ruehl win for supporting roles |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1992-03-31-mn-104-story.html |access-date=August 21, 2013 |date=March 31, 1992 |work=Los Angeles Times |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927135420/http://articles.latimes.com/1992-03-31/news/mn-104_1_jack-palance |archive-date=September 27, 2013 }}</ref> Other winners included ''[[Terminator 2: Judgment Day]]'' with four awards, ''[[Beauty and the Beast (1991 film)|Beauty and the Beast]]'', ''[[Bugsy]]'', and ''[[JFK (film)|JFK]]'' with two, and ''[[City Slickers]]'', ''[[Deadly Deception: General Electric, Nuclear Weapons and Our Environment]]'', ''[[The Fisher King]]'', ''[[In the Shadow of the Stars]]'', ''[[Manipulation (film)|Manipulation]]'', ''[[Mediterraneo]]'', ''[[Session Man (film)|Session Man]]'', and ''[[Thelma & Louise]]'' with one. The telecast garnered more than 44 million viewers in the United States.

== Winners and nominees ==
<!-- Please do not add any fact or statement below unless you have a credible source verifying it. Otherwise, it will be promptly removed. -->

The nominees for the 64th Academy Awards were announced on February 19, 1992, at 5:38&nbsp;a.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PST]] (13:38 [[UTC]]) at the [[Samuel Goldwyn Theater]] in [[Beverly Hills, California]], by [[Karl Malden]], president of the Academy, and actress [[Kathleen Turner]].<ref>{{cite news |last=O' Malley |first=Kathy |title=Here they come Word around New Hampshire is that the... |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1992/02/18/here-they-comeword-around-new-hampshire-is/ |access-date=August 25, 2013 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=February 18, 1992 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004223647/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/1992-02-18/news/9201150900_1_cuomo-write-in-effort-spin-patrol-new-hampshire |archive-date=October 4, 2013 }}</ref> ''[[Bugsy]]'' led all nominees with ten nominations; ''[[JFK (film)|JFK]]'' came in second with eight.<ref>{{cite news |last=Weinraub |first=Bernard |title='Bugsy' a Big Winner In Oscar Nominations Rife With Surprise |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1992/02/20/movies/bugsy-a-big-winner-in-oscar-nominations-rife-with-surprise.html |access-date=September 5, 2013 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=February 20, 1992 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005022754/http://www.nytimes.com/1992/02/20/movies/bugsy-a-big-winner-in-oscar-nominations-rife-with-surprise.html |archive-date=October 5, 2013 }}</ref>

The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on March 30, 1992. ''[[The Silence of the Lambs (film)|The Silence of the Lambs]]'' became the first horror film to win [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]] and the first film to be released on home video prior to winning that award.<ref name="BOO">{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=1170}}</ref> Moreover, it was the third film to win the "[[List of Big Five Academy Award winners and nominees|Big Five]]" major categories for picture, directing, lead acting performances, and screenwriting. The other two films to achieve this feat were 1934's ''[[It Happened One Night]]'' and 1975's ''[[One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest (film)|One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest]]''.<ref name="Seattle Times Oscar">{{cite news |last=Hartl |first=John |title='Silence' Makes Big Noise At Oscars -- In An Evening Of Firsts, Horror Film Walks Off With All Five Top Honors At Academy Awards |url=https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/19920331/1483921/silence-makes-big-noise-at-oscars----in-an-evening-of-firsts-horror-film-walks-off-with-all-five-top-honors-at-academy-awards |access-date=September 12, 2013 |work=[[The Seattle Times]] |date=March 31, 1992 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928054544/http://community.seattletimes.nwsource.com/archive/?date=19920331&slug=1483921 |archive-date=September 28, 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Weinraub |first=Bernard |title=Media Business; Can Ninja Turtle Owner Rescue Orion Pictures? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1992/04/01/business/media-business-can-ninja-turtle-owner-rescue-orion-pictures.html |access-date=August 23, 2013 |work=The New York Times |date=April 1, 1992 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130929042523/http://www.nytimes.com/1992/04/01/business/media-business-can-ninja-turtle-owner-rescue-orion-pictures.html |archive-date=September 29, 2013 }}</ref> ''[[Beauty and the Beast (1991 film)|Beauty and the Beast]]'' became the first animated film to be nominated for Best Picture<ref>{{cite news |last=Reardon |first=Patrick T. |title=Gaston A Figment Of '90s Animation |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1992/03/25/gaston-a-figment-of-90s-animation/ |access-date=August 26, 2013 |work=Chicago Tribune |date=March 25, 1992 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928185117/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/1992-03-25/news/9201270602_1_fairy-tale-gaston-betsy-hearne |archive-date=September 28, 2013 }}</ref> and the first film with three nominations for [[Academy Award for Best Original Song|Best Original Song]].<ref name="BOO"/> ''[[Boyz n the Hood]]'''s [[John Singleton]] became the first African-American to be nominated for Best Director and the youngest nominee in that category.<ref name="BOO" /> Nominated for Best Supporting Actress and Best Actress, respectively, [[Diane Ladd]] and [[Laura Dern]] became the first mother and daughter nominated in the same year.<ref name="BOO" />

== Ceremony information ==
[[File:Billy Crystal VF 2012 Shankbone.JPG|thumb|upright|[[Billy Crystal]] hosted the 64th Academy Awards.|alt=Photo of Billy Crystal in 2012.]]

Riding on the success of the [[63rd Academy Awards|previous year's ceremony]] which won several Emmys, AMPAS rehired [[Gil Cates]] for the third consecutive year.<ref>{{cite news |title='Cheers' Draws Cheers, 4 Emmys |url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/179875/CHEERS-DRAWS-CHEERS-4-EMMYS.html |access-date=September 9, 2013 |work=[[Deseret News]] |date=August 26, 1991 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921053414/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/179875/CHEERS-DRAWS-CHEERS-4-EMMYS.html |archive-date=September 21, 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Landis |first=Dave |title=More Misha |work=[[USA Today]] |date=October 10, 1991 |page=1D}}</ref> He christened the 1992 ceremony with the theme "Pure Joy of the Movies," explaining that "Motion pictures provide us with laughter, romance, adventure and a deeper understanding of ourselves. With all the extraordinary events that are taking place today, it's wonderful that we can still get away to see a film."<ref>{{cite news |last=McKerrow |first=Steve |title=Academy Awards Show Sign Of The Times |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/1992/03/30/academy-awards-show-sign-of-the-times/ |access-date=September 9, 2013 |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |date=March 30, 1992 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131015192612/http://articles.baltimoresun.com/1992-03-30/features/1992090098_1_academy-awards-show-cates-oscar |archive-date=October 15, 2013 }}</ref>

A month before the festivities, Cates recruited actor and comedian [[Billy Crystal]] to host the ceremony for the third straight year.<ref>{{cite news |title=Crystal back in the saddle as Oscar awards host |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=d75YAAAAIBAJ&pg=5173,2641263 |access-date=September 9, 2013 |work=[[The Gainesville Sun]] |date=February 9, 1992 |archive-date=February 25, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210225175124/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=d75YAAAAIBAJ&pg=5173,2641263 |url-status=live }}</ref> Shortly before the ceremony, Crystal got the flu, so Cates asked [[Tom Hanks]] for a possible replacement. Hanks agreed, but ultimately Crystal informed the producers that he would be able to host.<ref>{{cite news|last=Matthews |first=Jack |title=Commentary: Who Will Host the Oscars? It's Not Crystal Clear |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1994-01-22-ca-14265-story.html |access-date=December 7, 2013 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=January 22, 1994 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131218102251/http://articles.latimes.com/1994-01-22/entertainment/ca-14265_1_oscar-host |archive-date=December 18, 2013 }}</ref> According to ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' columnist [[Army Archerd]], Crystal planned to perform a bungee jump stunt as part of his entrance at the beginning of the ceremony. However, the act was scrapped due to high insurance costs for the AMPAS and Crystal coming down with the flu.<ref name="Stunt">{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=836}}</ref> Instead, Crystal, who was wearing [[Hannibal Lecter]]'s mask from ''[[The Silence of the Lambs (film)|The Silence of the Lambs]]'', was hauled onto the stage by two men.<ref name="Wiley 1996 840" />

Several other people were involved in the production of the ceremony. Choreographer [[Debbie Allen]] supervised the Best Song nominee performances and the Best Original Score dance number.<ref>{{cite news |last=Dunning |first=Jennifer |title=Television: Debbie Allen Chips Away At the Glass Ceiling |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1992/03/29/arts/television-debbie-allen-chips-away-at-the-glass-ceiling.html |access-date=September 10, 2013 |work=The New York Times |date=March 29, 1992 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150610230257/http://www.nytimes.com/1992/03/29/arts/television-debbie-allen-chips-away-at-the-glass-ceiling.html |archive-date=June 10, 2015 }}</ref> Film composer and musician [[Bill Conti]] served as musical director of the ceremony.<ref name="Conti">{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=845}}</ref> In tandem with the theme of the ceremony, [[Chuck Workman]] produced a montage highlighting famous comedy movie scenes from past and present.<ref name="Wiley 1996 840" />
=== Box office performance of nominees ===
At the time of the nominations announcement on February 19, the combined gross of the five Best Picture nominees at the US box office was $393&nbsp;million with an average of $78.7&nbsp;million per film.<ref name=BoxOfficeOscars>{{cite news |title=1991 Academy Award Nominations and Winner for Best Picture |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/oscar/chart/?yr=1991&p=.htm |access-date=September 5, 2013 |work=[[Box Office Mojo]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921053842/http://boxofficemojo.com/oscar/chart/?yr=1991&p=.htm |archive-date=September 21, 2013 }}</ref> ''The Silence of the Lambs'' was the highest earner among the Best Picture nominees, with $130.7&nbsp;million in domestic box office receipts.<ref name=BoxOfficeOscars /> The film was followed by ''Beauty and the Beast'' ($106.6&nbsp;million), ''The Prince of Tides'' ($59.3&nbsp;million), ''JFK'' ($58.1&nbsp;million), and finally ''Bugsy'' ($38.9&nbsp;million).<ref name=BoxOfficeOscars />

Of the 50 top-grossing movies of the year, 72 nominations went to 15 of them. Only ''Silence of the Lambs'' (3rd), ''Beauty and the Beast'' (6th), ''Cape Fear'' (10th), ''The Prince of Tides'' (18th), ''JFK'' (21st), ''Boyz n the Hood'' (22nd), ''Thelma and Louise'' (27th), ''The Fisher King'' (30th), and ''Bugsy'' (32nd) were nominated for Best Picture, directing, acting, or screenwriting. The other top 50 box office hits that earned nominations were ''Terminator 2: Judgment Day'' (1st), ''Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves'' (2nd), ''Hook'' (5th), ''The Addams Family'' (7th), ''Backdraft'' (12th), and ''Star Trek VI: the Undiscovery Country'' (13th).<ref>{{cite news |title=1991 Box Office Grosses (as of February 19, 1992) |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?asof=1992-02-19&view=releasedate&view2=domestic&yr=1991&sort=gross&order=DESC&p=.htm |access-date=February 14, 2014 |work=Box Office Mojo |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817072008/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?asof=1992-02-19&view=releasedate&view2=domestic&yr=1991&sort=gross&order=DESC&p=.htm |archive-date=August 17, 2016 }}</ref>

=== LGBT in film protest ===
Several days before the ceremony, [[LGBT]] activist groups such as [[Queer Nation]] and Out in Film announced plans to stage a protest outside the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]].<ref name="Protest">{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=834}}</ref> The organizations were voicing their complaints regarding derogatory and unflattering portrayals of homosexuals in film such as ''The Silence of the Lambs'', ''JFK'', and the upcoming film ''[[Basic Instinct]]''.<ref name="EW">{{cite magazine |last=Wells |first=Jeffrey |title=Up the Academy |url=https://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,309999,00.html |access-date=September 12, 2013 |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |date=March 27, 1992 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131003050529/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0%2C%2C309999%2C00.html |archive-date=October 3, 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Weir |first=John |title=Film: Gay-Bashing, Villainy and the Oscars |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1992/03/29/movies/film-gay-bashing-villainy-and-the-oscars.html |access-date=September 11, 2013 |work=The New York Times |date=March 29, 1992 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131002212107/http://www.nytimes.com/1992/03/29/movies/film-gay-bashing-villainy-and-the-oscars.html |archive-date=October 2, 2013 }}</ref> Queer Nation spokesman Rick Wilson said that the demonstrators "would stop cars from getting to the Oscars. It'll be a stall-in". Wilson also announced plans to disrupt the proceedings inside the theater.<ref name="Demonstration">{{cite news |last=Fox |first=David J. |title=What Impact on Oscar for Gay Protest?: Movies: Activists may stage disturbances at Academy Awards over demands for positive portrayals. |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1992-03-16-ca-2819-story.html |access-date=September 11, 2013 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=March 16, 1992 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221224721/http://articles.latimes.com/1992-03-16/entertainment/ca-2819_1_academy-awards |archive-date=February 21, 2015 }}</ref> In response, producer Gil Cates stated, "Anyone can protest about anything they want outside the show." But he said that the standard, "generic response" to something happening during the ceremony on camera, "would be to cut to a commercial."<ref name="Demonstration" /> Moreover, Academy spokesman Bob Werden reiterated that while security plans would not be as stringent as the previous year, firemen and police officers would be on hand in case of fallout from the protests.<ref name="EW" />

On the day of the telecast, several protesters carried various signs that contained statements such as "Stop Hollywood's Homophobia" and "Hollywood Stop Censoring Our True Queer Lives."<ref name="APO">{{harvnb|Levy|2003|p=354}}</ref> One man who had purchased tickets to the ceremony yelled statistics regarding [[AIDS]] in protest as [[John Candy]] was introducing a Best Song performance.<ref name="LGBT">{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=843}}</ref> Without making any arrests or having his comments heard during the broadcast, security immediately escorted the protester out.<ref name="APO" />

=== Critical reviews ===
The show received a positive reception from most media publications. ''[[The New York Times]]'' film critic [[Janet Maslin]] raved that the telecast was "uncharacteristically lively". She also praised host Crystal, saying that his opening monologue "set the evening's clever and iconoclastic tone."<ref>{{cite news |last=Maslin |first=Janet |title=Review/Television; A Very Different Oscars Broadcast |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1992/04/01/movies/review-television-a-very-different-oscars-broadcast.html |access-date=September 5, 2013 |work=The New York Times |date=April 1, 1992 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921054717/http://www.nytimes.com/1992/04/01/movies/review-television-a-very-different-oscars-broadcast.html |archive-date=September 21, 2013 }}</ref> Columnist Scott Williams of the [[Associated Press]] wrote that "Crystal was charming from the moment he was wheeled onstage and strolled into the audience wearing the face mask of the demonic Hannibal 'The Cannibal' Lecter from ''The Silence of the Lambs,'' which was named best picture."<ref>{{cite news |last=Williams |first=Scott |title=Cue the Shuttle: It's the 64th Annual Academy Awards With AM-Oscars, Bjt |url=https://apnews.com/e3e447a03c3dc9e22c4c876aeee7b44b |access-date=September 5, 2013 |work=[[Associated Press News]] |date=March 31, 1992 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921053437/http://www.apnewsarchive.com/1992/Cue-the-Shuttle-It-s-the-64th-Annual-Academy-Awards-With-AM-Oscars-Bjt/id-e3e447a03c3dc9e22c4c876aeee7b44b |archive-date=September 21, 2013 }}</ref> Ray Richmond from the ''[[Orange County Register]]'' commented that Crystal "is such a magnificent Oscar host that the job should be his as long as he wants it."<ref>{{cite news |last=Richmond |first=Ray |title=It's Crystal clear that comedian gilds the Oscars |work=[[Orange County Register]] |publisher=[[Freedom Communications]] |date=March 31, 1991 |page=F2}}</ref>

=== Ratings and reception ===
The American telecast on ABC drew in an average of 44.44 million people over its length, which was a 5% increase from the [[63rd Academy Awards|previous year's ceremony]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Johnson |first=Greg |title=Call It the Glamour Bowl |url=https://articles.latimes.com/1999/mar/18/business/fi-18458/2 |access-date=August 26, 2013 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=March 18, 1999 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928053918/http://articles.latimes.com/1999/mar/18/business/fi-18458/2 |archive-date=September 28, 2013 }}</ref> The show also drew higher [[Nielsen ratings]] compared to the previous ceremony, with 29.84% of households watching over a 50.26 share.<ref name="TVB Oscars">{{cite news |title=Academy Awards ratings |work=Television Bureau of Advertising |url=http://www.tvb.org/media/file/Academy_Awards.pdf |access-date=June 27, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130515152338/http://www.tvb.org/media/file/Academy_Awards.pdf |archive-date=May 15, 2013 }}</ref> In addition, it also drew a higher 18–49 demo rating with a 20.71 rating over a 39.51 share among viewers in that demographic.<ref name="TVB Oscars" />

In July 1992, the ceremony presentation received nine nominations at the [[44th Primetime Emmy Awards|44th Primetime Emmys]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Primetime Emmy Award database |url=http://www.emmys.com/shows/64th-annual-academy-awards |access-date=September 5, 2013 |publisher=[[Academy of Television Arts and Sciences]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203014913/http://www.emmys.com/shows/64th-annual-academy-awards |archive-date=December 3, 2013 }}</ref> The following month, the ceremony won three of those nominations for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Writing for a Variety Special|Outstanding Writing for a Variety Program]] ([[Hal Kanter]], [[Buz Kohan]], Billy Crystal, [[Marc Shaiman]], [[David Steinberg]], [[Robert Wuhl]], [[Bruce Vilanch]]), [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Music Direction|Outstanding Music Direction]] ([[Bill Conti]], [[Jack Eskew]], [[Julie Giroux]], Ashley Irwin, and [[Hummie Mann]]), and [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Costumes for a Variety, Nonfiction, or Reality Programming|Outstanding Costume Design for a Variety or Music Program]] (Raymond Aghayan).<ref>{{cite news |title=1992 Emmy Winners |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1992/09/01/news/1992-emmy-winners.html |access-date=September 5, 2013 |work=The New York Times |date=September 1, 1992 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131002203335/http://www.nytimes.com/1992/09/01/news/1992-emmy-winners.html |archive-date=October 2, 2013 }}</ref>
